title: Event Hub Capture Lag

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.39 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.39 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:metrics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" resourceType="Microsoft.EventHub/namespaces" metric_name="CaptureLag"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.39_event_hub_capture_lag_39"
| sort -_time
description: Capture to ADLS/Blob enables batch analytics; lag between enqueue and file availability delays downstream pipelines.
value: Detecting event hub capture lag early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Ingest CaptureLag from Azure Monitor. Alert when lag exceeds SLA (for example 10 minutes). Check storage throttling and capture file naming collisions. Scale throughput units if needed.
visualization: Line chart (capture lag), Table (namespace, lag minutes), Single value (worst lag).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:metrics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest CaptureLag from Azure Monitor. Alert when lag exceeds SLA (for example 10 minutes). Check storage throttling and capture file naming collisions. Scale throughput units if needed.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" resourceType="Microsoft.EventHub/namespaces" metric_name="CaptureLag"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.39_event_hub_capture_lag_39"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:metrics` in `index=azure` to detect event hub capture lag. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_39_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (capture lag), Table (namespace, lag minutes), Single value (worst lag)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of event hub capture lag so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
